summary: The round 2 fix adds one rule to merge3: a same-length hunk is merged line by line only when each base line that is anchored on a side sits at its own offset on that side. Any other same-length hunk becomes a single conflict, so a pick can no longer write a line twice or drop one. I traced the rule against the hunk boundaries. Each hunk starts just after a line anchored on both sides and stops at the next one, and the matching blocks are monotone. So the rule also rules out a side's line being anchored to a different base line in the hunk, and the Chalkboard adjacency case (one hand-edited line beside a template-changed line) still merges line by line. The new setup-test case covers a deletion and an addition in one hunk beside a template change, picked both ways. The README, the script header and the two standards were updated to match. The reviewer's guard refused setup-test.sh and python3, so this result comes from reading the code, not from running it, and there are no findings.
